chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Decca sessions with Rosetta Tharpe and gospel TV with Gatemouth Moore
summary: With Bobby Shad at Decca he recorded fifteen or sixteen sides a day, and later was the union musician on a gospel TV show.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, it's a subject that maybe we shouldn't be talking about, but an interesting one. You mentioned Rosetta Tharp last week, that you worked some with Sister Rosetta Tharp.

Yeah, I -- Bobby Shad was with Decca at that particular time. And we would go in the studio, he would go in the studio, and it was nothing for us to record 15 sides or 16 sides in a day, one right after the other. They'd just get the chord changes and then they would go ahead and do them.

Yeah, right. And I had -- well, like, gospel music. I did, on Channel 26 here, they had a gospel show -- and Gate mouth Moore. I don't know, do you remember him? He was a blues singer at one time, then he turned to be a minister.

So he had this show, and he would bring all of these gospel people in, and the union required them to have one union musician, so I was the musician. And then they brought their own organ player and piano player and I'd have to get the length of the tunes and all that straightened out with them and everything.
And I played with a lot of them. That's a strange
feeling, too, because they get in some terrible grooves.
